title: Guiding large language models to predict edit sequences for molecular synthesizability optimization
title_zh: 引导大型语言模型预测编辑序列以优化分子可合成性
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has revolutionized the exploration of chemical space, yet a critical bottleneck remains that a substantial fraction of generated molecules is synthetically inaccessible. Current solutions, such as post hoc filtering or projection-based methods, often compromise structural novelty or disrupt key pharmacophores by forcing molecules into predefined synthetic templates. Here we introduce SynCraft, a reasoning-based framework that reframes synthesizability optimization not as a sequence translation task but as a precise structural editing problem. Leveraging the emergent reasoning capabilities of large language models, SynCraft navigates the ‘synthesis cliff’ where minimal structural modifications yield substantial gains in synthetic feasibility. By predicting executable sequences of atom-level edits rather than generating SMILES strings directly, SynCraft circumvents the syntactic fragility of LLMs while harnessing their chemical intuition. Extensive benchmarks demonstrate that SynCraft outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in generating synthesizable analogues with high structural fidelity, with comparable performance across both proprietary and open-weight backends. Furthermore, through interaction-aware prompting, SynCraft successfully replicates expert medicinal chemistry intuition in editing PLK1 inhibitors and rescuing high-scoring RIPK1 candidates previously discarded in the molecular generation literature. For application convenience, we package the framework as an agent skill and demonstrate an end-to-end rescue workflow on candidate molecules generated for the SARS-CoV-2 main protease as an example. Computational drug design often generates molecules that cannot be synthesized. Li and Lai show how large language models can predict precise structural edits to fix these molecules, outperforming traditional methods and preserving key features.
abstract_zh: 生成式人工智能已彻底改变化学空间的探索，但仍存在关键瓶颈：生成的分子中有相当大一部分在合成上不可及。现有的解决方案，如事后过滤或基于投影的方法，往往通过强制分子进入预定义的合成模板，而牺牲了结构新颖性或破坏了关键的药效团。在此，我们引入SynCraft，一种基于推理的框架，将可合成性优化重新定义为精确的结构编辑问题，而非序列翻译任务。利用大型语言模型涌现的推理能力，SynCraft在‘合成悬崖’中导航，即最小的结构修饰可带来合成可行性的显著提升。通过预测原子级编辑的可执行序列，而不是直接生成SMILES字符串，SynCraft规避了LLM的语法脆弱性，同时利用了其化学直觉。广泛的基准测试表明，SynCraft在生成高结构保真度的可合成类似物方面优于最先进的基线方法，且在专有和开放权重后端上均表现相当。此外，通过交互感知提示，SynCraft成功复刻了专家医学化学编辑PLK1抑制剂的直觉，并挽救了在分子生成文献中被丢弃的高分RIPK1候选物。为了方便应用，我们将该框架打包为一个代理技能，并在SARS-CoV-2主蛋白候选分子的端到端救援工作流中进行了演示。计算药物设计常生成无法合成的分子。李和赵展示了大型语言模型如何预测精确的结构编辑来修复这些分子，优于传统方法并保留关键特征。
